frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The contraction/drawing-together of the face into a scowl — a hardening of the countenance into a grim, forbidding, displeased aspect (the "frowning-grimness" residue).

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The contraction/drawing-together of the face into a scowl — a hardening of the countenance into a grim, forbidding, displeased aspect (the "frowning-grimness" residue).
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all three occurrences the root supplies one invariant: the countenance drawn tight into a grim, forbidding scowl. (1) 74:22:2:1 ثُمَّ عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ — a human agent "scowled and glared"; عَبَسَ is the facial contraction itself, reinforced by its pairing with بَسَرَ (glaring/grimacing look). (2) 80:1:1:1 عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ — again a human "scowled and turned away"; here the root delivers the same facial scowl, while the distinct act of aversion is carried by the separate verb تَوَلَّى (not by ع ب س). (3) 76:10:6:1 يَوْمًا عَبُوسًا قَمْطَرِيرًا — the intensive adjective عَبُوس ("scowling/grim") is predicated of a Day; a Day has no literal face, so the facial-scowl residue is transferred metaphorically to characterize the Day as grim/forbidding in aspect, reinforced by قَمْطَرِير (distressful/harsh). The same grim-forbidding contraction underlies the verbal act (forms 1-2) and the attributive quality (form 3).
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Subtracting layers: (a) FORM — Form-I verb عَبَسَ names the act of scowling (74:22, 80:1); the ADJ/intensive عَبُوس names the enduring quality "grim/scowling" (76:10); the root residue (facial-grim contraction) is constant across verb vs. adjective. (b) CONSTRUCTION — 74:22 and 80:1 are bare intransitive verbs coordinated with a second verb (بَسَرَ / تَوَلَّى); 76:10 is an attributive adjective modifying يَوْمًا. These frames add coordination and attribution but not the core meaning. (c) PARTICIPANTS — subject is a human displeased agent in 74:22 (a rejecter) and 80:1 (the one who turned from the blind man); in 76:10 the bearer is a Day, forcing metaphorical transfer of the facial residue. (d) CONTEXT — polemical/narrative (74, 80) vs. eschatological (76); context supplies the target of grimness (rejection vs. a dreaded Day) but not the residue. What remains after subtraction in every case: the grim, forbidding contraction of aspect.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 76:10:6:1 (يَوْمًا عَبُوسًا) is hardest: a Day cannot literally contract its face. It reconciles by internally-attested metaphorical extension — عَبُوس is the intensive adjectival form of the very scowling act seen verbally in 74:22 and 80:1, and here transfers the "grim/forbidding countenance" to the Day, a transfer reinforced by the paired harshness word قَمْطَرِير. The bridge (facial grimness → grim aspect of an entity) is supported by the shared root-form and does not require external lexicon.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative core is "displeasure/aversion" (an emotional/behavioral residue rather than a physical-facial one). Internal evidence arbitrates against it: in 80:1 the aversive act ("turned away") is carried by a separate coordinated verb تَوَلَّى, showing ع ب س is NOT itself the turning-away/aversion but the facial contraction preceding it; likewise in 74:22 it pairs with بَسَرَ, another countenance/look verb, keeping the meaning on the face rather than on abstract emotion. The physical facial-grimness reading is thus more surface-anchored, with displeasure being a downstream implication rather than the residue.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors: بَسَرَ (b-s-r, glaring/grimacing look — co-occurs in 74:22, denotes the hostile stare rather than the facial contraction); قَطَبَ (q-T-b, knitting the brows); كَلَحَ (k-l-H, grimacing with drawn-back lips); and the aversion roots تَوَلَّى / أَعْرَضَ (turning away — behavioral, co-occurs in 80:1). ع ب س is distinct as the contraction/gathering of the face into a grim scowl (the whole-countenance darkening), separable from the eyes'/gaze glare (بسر), from brow-knitting (قطب), and from bodily turning-away (تولى). Falsifiability: if a confirmed عبس occurrence required a meaning of pure emotional aversion or bodily turning-away with no possible facial-grimness/forbidding-aspect reading, the facial-contraction core would fail.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty residue — the grim, forbidding contraction of the countenance into a scowl — is recoverable in all three occurrences. It is surface-literal in the two verbal cases (74:22, 80:1), where careful layer-subtraction shows the root supplies the facial scowl while coordinated verbs supply the glare/turning-away. The third case (76:10) is the adjectival/intensive عَبُوس applied to a Day, where the residue is present only by a well-supported metaphorical extension (grim-faced → grim/forbidding aspect), bridged by the shared root-form and the reinforcing قَمْطَرِير. Because unity holds cleanly for two occurrences but the third requires reconciled metaphorical transfer rather than surface literality, the disposition is PREFERRED at MODERATE strength: the conceptual center is determinate and sharply distinct from neighbor roots, but not surface-recoverable in all three without inferential extension. No occurrence remains unreconciled; inconsistent_refs is empty.

adversarial_verification.notes: Adversarial sweep over all 3 occurrences found no genuine failing case. (1) 74:22 عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ and (2) 80:1 عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ are literal human facial contraction into a scowl; the discovery correctly assigns only the frown to ع ب س, letting the paired verbs (بسر glaring, تولّى turning away) carry their own distinct acts. Hardest case is (3) 76:10 يَوْمًا عَبُوسًا قَمْطَرِيرًا, where the intensive adjective is predicated of a faceless Day; this requires metaphorical transfer, but يوم عبوس ("grim/frowning day") is a standard lexicalized Arabic metonymy — a routine attributive extension of the countenance-contraction sense, reinforced by قمطرير, not an ad-hoc rescue or a separate homonym. Distinctiveness: ع ب س (contraction/darkening of the countenance into displeasure) discriminates cleanly against its co-occurring neighbor بسر (the glaring/hostile look) — the two pair in 74:22 precisely because complementary — and against قطب (drawing brows together). Falsifiability: failure condition = a Quranic use in an unrelated sense (e.g., the classical noun for dried dung on a camel's tail); no such use appears, and all 3 tokens are the frown sense, so nothing meets the failure condition. No semantic split or homonymy to bridge; unity is distinct and falsifiable.

occurrence_dispositions.note: عَبَسَ = the human agent's face contracted into a scowl; reinforced by paired وَبَسَرَ (glaring/grimacing). Facial-scowl residue directly present.

عَبَسَ = the agent scowled; facial contraction residue present, the separate aversion act being carried by وَتَوَلَّىٰ rather than by ع ب س.
